headline: Approved a grant agreement for pedestrian access to Casavant Natural Area and ten thousand dollars from the training reserve fund for staff training.
summary: Council approved the consent agenda and a grant agreement for pedestrian access to the Casavant Natural Area. It approved ten thousand dollars from the training reserve fund for staff training. Council discussed a longevity bonus pay policy and a leave pool policy, and asked existing commissions for input on changing the commission structure.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including prior minutes, payroll and accounts payable warrants, and routine items, 4-0.
Approved the City Manager executing a Vermont Community Development Program grant agreement for pedestrian access to the Casavant Natural Area, 4-0.
Approved using ten thousand dollars from the training reserve fund for employee training and professional development, unanimously 4-0.
Approved a motion to seek input from existing commissions on possible changes to the commission structure, 4-0. No vote was taken to change the structure.

Motion carried 4-0.

Motion: A motion to approve the use of ten thousand dollars from the training reserve fund to support employee training and professional development opportunities made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed unanimously 4-0.

Motion: A motion to seek input from existing commissions on the discussion that we’ve had tonight that will be guided by the memo that the Deputy Mayor and Mayor will provide to Council no later than next Wednesday made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0.

Motion: Motion to approve the Consent Agenda made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor 
Goodrich. Motion passed unanimously 4-0. 
V. Council Reports 
Mayor Thomas Renner: The Planning Commission will be meeting this Thursday at 6:30 at City Hall. 
You can also watch online. As always, I encourage folks to attend Planning Commission meetings. There 
is a lot of work that gets done there with what our city looks like and what it will look like which is very 
important to a lot of residents, so I encourage your attendance. 
 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf: I want to thank the Councilors for covering for me while I was away in August 
and Safe, Healthy, Connected People has been cancelled due to a lack of agenda items. The Housing 
Commission has been cancelled for the same reason. CSWD will meet at its regular time on the fourth 
Wednesday of the month at 6 PM at their offices in Williston or available online. The agenda for that 
will be posted the week before the meeting. 
 
Councilor Al Turkos: On both August 5th and September 2nd, the Burlington Airport Commission met. I 
want to remind folks that on September 21st later this month, the team from the Burlington Airport will 
be here to update Winooski residents. I’ve also had a few Colchester residents reach out, so 
neighboring residents are obviously welcome to attend as well and the team from the airport will 
specifically updating us around the Sound Mitigation work that they’re doing. That is on our next City 
Council meeting on September 21st. 
 
The Downtown Winooski board met on Wednesday, August 19th, and we are preparing for our next 
event which will be next Wednesday, September 16th, which is our annual Winooski Pride event. This is 
an event that is welcome to all ages, families, everyone should come, new UVM students are welcome 
to come. We will have DJs; Specs will be there distributing drinks. We have food. I will be there and is 
one of my favorite events outside of Halloween. I highly recommend that if everyone is around, you 
should come. 
 
Other things that I want to highlight were the Winooski School District held an amazing back to school 
barbecue that Councilor Goodrich, Councilor Ogilvie, myself, Elaine, our amazing City Manager were 
there. I want to thank that partnership between us and the school district. We’ve had an easy back to 
school. I have been a greater in the mornings and it’s been wonderful to see the kiddos and open the 
doors for them. Pre-K started today, which has been great.  
 
I want to give a big shoutout to the Winooski Community Services Department. I joined them on 
Thursday, August 13th, for a Landry Park Cleanup. Sidra, who is our Parks and Trails Steward, has been 
doing an amazing job organizing these and we met and potentially talked about doing a bird walk. They 
have been doing some amazing work, and I am super grateful for them. 
 
This Saturday, September 12th, at 8:30 AM, I am organizing our new Winooski Cleanup Crew. We’ll be 
meeting outside of Specs at 8:30 at 7 West Canal Street. This is the second time we’re doing this. It 
was so successful in the month of August that folks asked me to bring it back. I will be distributing latex 
gloves, garbage bags, buckets, etc. We do a loop around the circle and distribute off into other 
neighborhoods as well. If folks are interested, I posted it on Front Porch Forum, or you can follow up 
with me directly. It’s really about keeping our city clean, and we pick up trash, meet neighbors, and 
connect.

Councilor Elsie Goodrich: The Finance Commission met on August 18th. The first order of business was 
electing a new secretary, so thank you to Autumn Crabtree. The primary topic of the meeting was a 
discussion around the community outreach efforts for the economic vitality section of the 
Comprehensive Plan Open House series. Since we had low turnout and limited public feedback for that 
section, the commission brainstormed some improvements and ideas while recognizing the limitations 
the city has to actually implement those. Members suggested after the process is done, the city could 
debrief and reflect on what worked for outreach to reflect and improve future engagement. Their next 
meeting is scheduled for Tuesday, September 15th. I covered the Housing Commission meeting for 
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf at the August 25th meeting. The Housing Commission received a presentation 
from the Director of Planning on the Building Typologies Report and a presentation from the Housing 
Director on the fiscal year 2026 landlord survey. One of the primary takeaways of that survey is that 
Winooski’s rental housing markets seems to be less competitive than it was last year, suggesting some 
easing of market pressures compared to recent years. Due to low attendance, the other items were 
postponed until a later meeting. 
 
Councilor Eli Ogilvie: On August 27th, the Municipal Infrastructure Commission met, and we had some 
wonderful conversations. We spent a majority of the meeting discussing infrastructure and what’s been 
working and what hasn’t been. The commission also was updated on a citywide traffic calming study 
that was conducted this summer. The city expects to receive the final report in the coming months. 
Lastly, we reviewed the DPW fiscal year 2027 priority list. If folks would like to read more about the 
commission’s discussions, the unofficial minutes are posted on the Winooski City website. 
 
VI. City Updates 
 
E
laine Wang, City Manager, gave the following updates 
 
Many thanks to everyone who attended and provided feedback during the Comprehensive Plan Open House 
series of events this summer. If you could not attend, or are new to this process, the City of Winooski must 
readopt a municipal plan (a high-level plan that guides the City's future) by the end of 2027. The current plan, 
known as the Master Plan, is being updated and will be called the "Comprehensive Plan".  
 
Community feedback is needed to guide the Comprehensive Plan. Please take a moment to fill out a 
community survey by visiting winooskivt.gov/plan. There is one survey per area, including: 
 
• Land Use Goals and Actions (How does Winooski change and grow?  
• Municipal Infrastructure (How does Winooski improve our water, sewer, stormwater, transportation, and 
energy network?) 
• Economic Vitality (How does Winooski maintain/expand our economy?) 
• Safe, Healthy, Connected People How does Winooski improve livability, parks, community programs, 
health, and safety? 
• For context, there is no survey for the Housing section, as it is being shaped by the ongoing Housing Needs 
Assessment process 
Road repair and resurfacing began today and will occur until September 18th, which includes Brisson Court, 
North St., Cedar St., Dufresne Drive, and Pine Grove Terrace. For details about this work including the 
schedule, traffic impacts, parking restrictions, and driveway access, please visit winooskivt.gov/news.

VII. Regular Items 
A. Discussion/Approval: Grant Agreement with Vermont Community Development Program for 
Pedestrian Access to Casavant Natural Area to Reimburse Nedde Real Estate for Eligible Construction 
Costs, and Related Council Actions Needed - Jon Rauscher, Director of Public Works 
 
Minutes: City Manager Wang spoke on behalf of the Public Works Director about the grant agreement 
related to improving pedestrian access to the Casavant Natural Area. The City Manager reviewed the 
timeline of the project for Lot 7D, which was previously approved by Council, and this new access will 
now be of higher quality and accessible to those with mobility challenges. The grant outlines specific 
guidelines that the City must adhere to, and Council is responsible for signing off on the expectations 
and approval to allow the developer to be reimbursed for the work done. The Mayor reiterated the 
financial responsibility for the development and mentioned that with this grant, this access with be cost 
neutral for the City. 
 
Council had some follow-up questions related to the timeframe for completion as well as defining what 
cost-neutrality means on behalf of city staff. The City Manager was able to provide clarifying answers.   
 
Motion: Motion to approve the City Manager to execute the VCDP grant agreement for improvements 
related to pedestrian access to the Casavant Natural Area contingent on executing the agreement 
between the city and Nedde Real Estate that ensures grant compliance, if needed by Councilor Turkos 
and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion carried 4-0. 
B. Discussion: Introduction - Non-Union Longevity Bonus Pay Policy - Jesse Acri, Human Resources 
Director 
Minutes: The Human Resources Director spoke about the proposed policy related to city staff who have 
already reached their maximum step allowance in their pay range. Employees are given a cost-of-living 
allowance increase each year, as well as a step increase, but those who no longer have additional steps 
do not get extra compensation compared to those who increase in their step range. Tim Cece asked the 
Council about previous policies the City had as well as how the numerical amount was established in 
this new policy, as well as questions about COLA increases overall. This policy is already in place 
previously for both employees that participate in ASFCME as well as the Police Union, and this proposed 
policy matches their language as well. 
Discussion ensued amongst the Council and City Staff, as this proposed policy cannot be adopted 
immediately, and needs time for members of the public to give possible feedback. With this discussion, 
this item can be brought to the Council at the next meeting for approval. The Council shared their 
opinions around this policy and were able to ask any questions. The City Manager asked Council for an 
inclination of support at the end of the discussion. 
C. Discussion: Leave Pool Policy - Jessi Acri, Human Resources Director 
Minutes: The Human Resources Director reviewed the possible new policy as there is no current formal 
policy in place and would create a consistent process that aligns with the current policies in place.  
A conversation with Council and City Staff followed the introduction of the policy related to current 
policies already in place and its rationale. Currently, the City has a sick leave policy in place as well as a 
sick leave bank for those that may need additional hours. Questions regarding the importance of

utilizing time off through already established policies in place and questioned the need for establishing 
this new policy. All members of the Council shared their thoughts with additional questions throughout 
this discussion. In addition, Tom Buckley gave public comments and asked the Council whether this 
policy is the same for union and non-union employees and whether there is an opportunity for 
disparities during further conversations, with the Human Resources director stating it would apply for 
everyone. 
The Mayor described hearing a desire to review the current leave pool policy, as the idea of establishing 
a temporary new policy had mixed opinions on behalf of Council members. In addition, Council asked if 
staff had an opportunity to review this policy and the Human Resources Director stated no feedback 
was received. At the end of the discussion, the City Manager thanked Council for their concerns about 
City Staff. 
D. Discussion/Approval: Reserve Request: Supplement Training Budget - Jesse Acri, Human Resources     
Director 
Minutes: The Human Resources Director reviewed the reserve request with Council, asking for an 
additional ten thousand dollars for supplementing the training budget this current fiscal year. This is 
traditionally reviewed during budget discussions, but training opportunities for staff have exceeded this 
year’s current allotted amount. The Finance Director clarified they are asking for more than is currently 
needed but allows for a buffer in case further training comes up during this fiscal year. Currently there 
it isn’t expected that this trend will continue in the following fiscal year. 
 
Questions were raised by the Council related to which specific funding this will be taken from, especially 
as the Mayor made mention they have concerns about moving money from the reserve accounts, with 
City Staff being able to share more clarifying information. Questions related to per diem and mileage 
reimbursement were reviewed as those amounts are updated by the Federal Government and at 
different times throughout the year. 
 
Motion: A motion to approve the use of ten thousand dollars from the training reserve fund to support 
employee training and professional development opportunities made by Councilor Turkos and seconded 
by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed unanimously 4-0. 
 
The Council took a recess from 7:19 PM and continued the meeting at 7:26 PM. 
E. Discussion/Approval: Boards, Committees, and Commission Structure - Deputy Mayor Bryn Oakleaf 
Minutes: The Mayor started the discussion by thanking the Deputy Mayor’s leadership on this item. This 
current commission structure was created during the last Master Plan and is asking for revisions as the 
City works to develop the upcoming Comprehensive Plan. The Mayor continued to acknowledge that 
these bodies are useful for the City and wants to ensure that in the future it remains an engaging 
process and ensure that the continued work is useful. 
 
A memo created by the Mayor and Deputy Mayor outlined possible alternatives to the current 
commission structure and the Council had an extensive discussion with a chance to give feedback on 
what each believes would work best. Other possible alternatives included in the discussion were to 
possibly have one ad-hoc committee which would take all (except for the Planning Commission and 
Development Review Board as these must remain separate unless having a joint meeting) important 
topics at the present moment to have a larger conversation related to whatever the current needs are.

Another alternative would be to merge some of the commissions (e.g. the Inclusion and Belonging 
Commission joining with the Safe, Healthy, People Commission).  
 
Throughout the Council discussion, the need to review these alternatives with each commission at their 
next meetings was important to guide any changes to the current structure. Most Councilors agree on a 
commission model and did not want to move forward with the first idea presented in the memo (e.g., 
having a ward model), and the Mayor agrees that feedback should be solicited from all commissions 
before determining any next steps. The Mayor and Deputy Mayor agreed that they can update the 
current memo to reflect the discussion before the next council meeting. No vote was taken to change 
the commission structure. 
 
Motion: A motion to seek input from existing commissions on the discussion that we’ve had tonight that 
will be guided by the memo that the Deputy Mayor and Mayor will provide to Council no later than next 
Wednesday made by Councilor Turkos and seconded by Councilor Goodrich. Motion passed 4-0. 
 
VIII. Adjourn 
 
Motion: Motion to adjourn at 8:41 PM made by Deputy Mayor Oakleaf and seconded by Councilor 
Turkos. Motion passed 4-0.
